papers.title_in_file: Approximation and Generalization Capacities of Parametrized Quantum Circuits for Functions in Sobolev Spaces
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper proving that parametrized quantum circuits can approximate continuous, p-integrable and Sobolev-space functions, with generalization bounds.

assertions.value: The paper proves that parametrized quantum circuits can arbitrarily approximate the space of continuous functions, the space of p-integrable functions and the Hk space of functions whose derivatives up to order k are square integrable.
quotes: arbitrarily approximate the space of continuous functions, the space of p-integrable functions and the Hk space, which is the set of functions whose derivatives up to order k are square integrable
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorems 2, 3 and 4, pp.5-6; proofs in Appendix A

assertions.value: The authors state that the approximation results assume the trainable circuit blocks can represent arbitrary global unitaries, and that this may require exponential circuit depth.
quotes: are able to represent arbitrary global unitaries. In practice, this may require exponential circuit depth.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 2 states the assumption, p.4
assertions.reader_inference: The approximation results are existence results, not a statement about circuits of practical size.

assertions.value: The authors state that convergence in the L2 sense does not imply other modes of convergence.
quotes: Note that convergence in the L2 sense does not imply other modes of convergence.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 2 remark after Theorem 1, p.4

papers.title_in_file: Contextual Quantum Neural Networks for Stock Price Prediction
papers.what_it_is: A Fujitsu study applying a quantum multi-task learning circuit to predict binary stock-move distributions, tested in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that the KL divergences in the multi-task learning case are lower than in the single-task case, and attribute this to correlations captured between the Apple and Google datasets.
assertions.anchor: Section VI.C and Table I, p.15
quotes: Table 1 further confirms this, showing that the KL Divergences in the multi-task learning case are lower.
We attribute this improvement to correlations captured between the Apple and Google datasets
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study in simulation; the cause is the authors' attribution
assertions.reader_inference: Two stocks and binary up/down targets; the result does not show a gain on a trading or fraud task.

assertions.value: The authors state that the simulations use Apple stock data discretized to binary values, 0 for a price decrease and 1 for an increase.
quotes: discretized to binary values where 0 indicates a price decrease, and 1 indicates an increase
assertions.certainty_reason: Section VI.A states the setup, p.14

assertions.value: The authors state that classical deep learning models can outperform quantum approaches in conventional large-scale time-series prediction tasks.
quotes: It is important to note, however, that classical deep learning models can outperform quantum approaches in conventional large-scale time-series prediction tasks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section VI.C, p.15: the paper's own statement of scope

papers.title_in_file: Re-QGAN: an optimized adversarial quantum circuit learning framework
papers.what_it_is: A quantum GAN design using real Hilbert spaces and stereographic-projection encoding, tested on small MNIST subsets with 2 to 4 qubits.

assertions.value: The authors report that re-qGAN generated samples the discriminator could not detect by the 15th epoch, and say recent proposals generally require around 100 epochs.
quotes: the re-qGAN could generate undetectably (from the discriminator viewpoint) samples at the 15th epoch cycle
which generally require around 100 epochs to generate undetectable samples
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on a small MNIST subset; the 100-epoch comparison is cited from other work

assertions.value: The authors state that the experiments use 25 epochs, a subset of 20 images from the MNIST dataset, and a reduced number of qubits from 2 to 4.
quotes: we consider 25 epochs and a subset of 20 images from the MNIST to generate a new digit
we consider a reduced number of qubits (from 2 to 4)
assertions.certainty_reason: Section I states the experiment setup, p.4

assertions.value: The authors report that the generated digit's resolution and quality do not scale with the number of qubits.
quotes: the generated digit's resolution and quality do not scale with the number of qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: Section I, p.4: the paper states this limit of its results

papers.title_in_file: Precise Image Generation on Current Noisy Quantum Computing Devices
papers.what_it_is: A CERN and DESY study of the Quantum Angle Generator, a full quantum generative model for calorimeter shower images, with a noise study on simulators and IBM hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report that training with noise gave stable results until 3% noise, against until 1.5% noise when noise was applied in inference only.
quotes: training the models with noise leads to better performance (stable until 3% noise)
applying noise in inference only (stable until 1.5% noise)
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study and one model

assertions.value: The authors report that during training on ibmq montreal the readout noise of one qubit increased to 8%, and that the model recovered and adapted to the new noisy environment.
quotes: the readout noise of one qubit increased to 8%
the model recovered and adapted to the new noisy environment
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical observation from one training run on one device

assertions.value: The authors report that inference accuracy on the real quantum hardware was worse than the simulation predicted, as indicated by a larger MSE value.
quotes: The accuracy on the real hardware is worse than predicted by the simulation, as indicated by a larger MSE value.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one device

papers.title_in_file: eXplainable AI for Quantum Machine Learning
papers.what_it_is: A d-fine paper testing black-box explainers on parametrized quantum circuits and proposing qSHAP, an explainability method specific to such circuits.

assertions.value: The authors propose qSHAP, an xAI method specifically designed for parametrized quantum circuits, and state that for qSHAP the adverse effect of noise is considerably reduced compared to the other explainers.
quotes: we propose qSHAP, which is an xAI method specifically designed for PQCs.
For qSHAP, the adverse effect of noise is considerably reduced compared to the other explainers.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from the paper's own experiments

assertions.value: The authors state that qSHAP does not resolve the exponential scaling, and that it scales exponentially with the number of features rather than the number of qubits.
quotes: Please note that this algorithm does not resolve issues related to the exponential scaling.
the algorithm does not scale exponentially with respect to the number of qubits, but with respect to the number of features.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section VI states the limit of qSHAP

assertions.value: The authors state that the drawback of standard black-box xAI models is their exponential scaling and their behaviour under the noise of NISQ devices.
quotes: The drawback of these standard black-box xAI models is their exponential scaling and their behaviour under the noise of NISQ devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim in the conclusion

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Architecture Search with Unsupervised Representation Learning
papers.what_it_is: A quantum architecture search framework that learns circuit representations without labels and searches them with REINFORCE and Bayesian optimization.

assertions.value: The authors state that the framework decouples unsupervised architecture representation learning from the search process, so learned representations can be reused across downstream tasks, and that it removes the need for a predictor trained on large labeled datasets.
quotes: we decouple unsupervised architecture representation learning from the search process, enabling learned representations to be reused across different downstream tasks
we eliminate the need for a predictor trained on large labeled datasets
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 1 states the design of the framework, p.2

assertions.value: The authors report that both MaxCut circuits retained their optimal output performance when transferred from simulator to real hardware, with 100% probability of measuring the optimal bitstring in 10,000 repeated shots.
quotes: both MaxCut circuits retained their optimal output performance when transferred from simulator to real hardware
The circuits achieved a 100% probability of measuring the optimal bitstring in 10,000 repeated shots
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result on two small circuits on one device

assertions.value: The authors report that their encoding method achieves the highest search efficiency in most cases, although performance on the 12-qubit task is slightly lower than with another encoding method.
quotes: In most cases, our encoding method achieves the highest search efficiency, although the performance for the 12-qubit task is slightly lower than with another encoding method.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study

papers.title_in_file: Classification and emergence of quantum spin liquids in chiral Rydberg models
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction and keyword search of the full text for quantum computing, machine learning and qubit; conclusion section located but not needed.
papers.what_it_is: A condensed-matter physics paper classifying chiral spin liquids on the honeycomb lattice and comparing parton wavefunctions with Rydberg-model ground states.
papers.why_not: The paper studies quantum spin liquid phases in a Rydberg-atom Hamiltonian. It has no quantum computing workload, no machine learning content and no finance content.

papers.title_in_file: Geometric Quantum Machine Learning with Horizontal Quantum Gates
papers.what_it_is: A Xanadu paper proposing horizontal quantum gates, built from homogeneous spaces, as a less restrictive alternative to equivariant circuits in geometric QML.

assertions.value: The authors report that a circuit of horizontal gates can find the ground state of an SU(2)-symmetric model where the ground state spin sector is unknown, a task where they say equivariant circuits fall short.
quotes: a circuit comprised of horizontal gates can find the ground state of an SU(2)-symmetric model where the ground state spin sector is unknown
task where equivariant circuits fall short
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from numerical simulation of one model

assertions.value: The authors state that the SU(4)/U(3) gates they considered are significantly more efficient than general SU(4) gates, with a quadratic reduction in the number of parameters for a generic problem.
assertions.anchor: Abstract and Section 6, p.1 and p.12
quotes: we have shown that the SU(4)/U(3) gates we considered are significantly more efficient when compared to general SU(4) gates
achieving a quadratic reduction in the number of parameters for a generic problem
assertions.certainty_reason: Efficiency is shown numerically for the gate class considered

assertions.value: The authors state that the resulting blocks of horizontal gates can still be expensive to implement with a standard gate set.
quotes: the resulting blocks of gates can still be expensive to implement with a standard gate set
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 6 states this limit of the construction
